description: Curated Gene Fitness SNP panel for Yeliztli (P3-45). Covers 4 fitness pathways (Endurance, Power, Recovery & Injury, Training Response) with 8 curated SNPs plus GWAS Catalog fitness EFO term associations. ACTN3 R577X uses three-state calling (RR/RX/XX). ACE rs4341 is an I/D proxy with coverage caveat.

pathways.name: Endurance
pathways.description: Variants influencing aerobic capacity, mitochondrial biogenesis, and sustained endurance performance.

CC.effect_summary: RR genotype — functional alpha-actinin-3 in fast-twitch muscle fibers. Associated with power and sprint performance.

CT.effect_summary: RX genotype — one functional copy of alpha-actinin-3, so the protein is present, unlike the XX deficiency; expression is intermediate, consistent with an additive model. Genotype alone does not predict individual power or endurance aptitude: RX does not discriminate between power and endurance athletes, and reported associations vary by ancestry, sex, athlete status, and study design. Context-only.

TC.effect_summary: RX genotype — one functional copy of alpha-actinin-3, so the protein is present, unlike the XX deficiency; expression is intermediate, consistent with an additive model. Genotype alone does not predict individual power or endurance aptitude: RX does not discriminate between power and endurance athletes, and reported associations vary by ancestry, sex, athlete status, and study design. Context-only.

TT.effect_summary: XX genotype — complete absence of alpha-actinin-3 in fast-twitch fibers, a common loss-of-function shift in muscle physiology. XX is consistently under-represented among sprint/power athletes (i.e. reduced sprint/power potential); a human endurance-performance advantage is NOT established — large endurance-athlete cohorts and meta-analyses show no consistent XX endurance benefit. Context-only, not an elevated endurance call.

snps.recommendation_text: ACTN3 R577X is among the most-studied sport-performance variants, but it is a weak, non-predictive marker. The consistently-replicated signal is reduced sprint/power potential for XX (and a power/sprint tendency for RR); an XX endurance advantage is not established in human studies. Genotype should not guide training choices in place of observed performance and training response.

GG.effect_summary: Normal PPARGC1A (PGC-1α) activity. Standard mitochondrial biogenesis and aerobic capacity.

GA.effect_summary: One copy of Ser482 variant. Mildly reduced PGC-1α activity. May have modestly lower baseline VO2max.

AG.effect_summary: One copy of Ser482 variant. Mildly reduced PGC-1α activity. May have modestly lower baseline VO2max.

AA.effect_summary: Homozygous Ser482. Reduced PGC-1α activity. Associated with lower baseline aerobic capacity and VO2max, though endurance training can still improve fitness.

snps.recommendation_text: PPARGC1A Gly482Ser has been associated with VO2max variation. Regular aerobic exercise can improve endurance capacity regardless of genotype.

CC.effect_summary: Normal AMP deaminase 1 activity. Standard purine nucleotide cycle in exercising muscle.

CT.effect_summary: Carrier of AMPD1 deficiency allele. Mildly reduced AMP deaminase activity. Some individuals report earlier muscle fatigue during intense exercise.

TC.effect_summary: Carrier of AMPD1 deficiency allele. Mildly reduced AMP deaminase activity. Some individuals report earlier muscle fatigue during intense exercise.

TT.effect_summary: Homozygous AMPD1 deficiency. Absent AMP deaminase in skeletal muscle. May experience exercise-induced myalgia and premature fatigue.

snps.recommendation_text: AMPD1 deficiency is common (~2% homozygous in Europeans). Symptoms vary widely — many homozygous individuals are asymptomatic. Adjust exercise intensity if exercise-induced cramping occurs.

pathways.name: Power
pathways.description: Variants influencing explosive strength, fast-twitch muscle fiber composition, and sprint performance.

AA.effect_summary: Proxy for ACE II genotype (insertion/insertion). Reported in some meta-analyses as enriched in elite endurance athletes; evidence is sport-specific and heterogeneous.

AG.effect_summary: Proxy for ACE ID genotype (insertion/deletion). Intermediate ACE activity; performance evidence is mixed and not deterministic.

GA.effect_summary: Proxy for ACE ID genotype (insertion/deletion). Intermediate ACE activity; performance evidence is mixed and not deterministic.

GG.effect_summary: Proxy for ACE DD genotype (deletion/deletion). Often discussed for power/sprint phenotypes, but the association is modest, population-specific, and heterogeneous (some cohorts find DD unfavourable for power or enriched in endurance), and the largest meta-analysis finds no overall genomic-variant association with performance. Treated as contextual, not a strong (Elevated) signal.

snps.coverage_note: rs4341 is a proxy SNP for the ACE insertion/deletion (I/D) polymorphism, which is a 287 bp Alu repeat not directly genotyped on SNP arrays. Published genotyping studies report high linkage disequilibrium with ACE I/D in specific cohorts, but proxy accuracy may vary by ancestry and assay.
snps.recommendation_text: Treat ACE I/D as contextual, research-grade fitness information only. Some endurance-modality meta-analyses report enrichment of the II genotype, while broader meta-analysis finds no overall genomic-variant association with power or endurance performance; do not make deterministic training recommendations from this variant alone.

TT.effect_summary: MCT1 rs1049434 TT (reference). MCT1 (SLC16A1) facilitates lactate transport across muscle-cell membranes.

TA.effect_summary: One copy of the MCT1 rs1049434 (Asp490Glu) variant. Associated with genotype-dependent differences in lactate transport/clearance during high-intensity exercise; the direction and performance impact are debated and cohort-dependent.

AT.effect_summary: One copy of the MCT1 rs1049434 (Asp490Glu) variant. Associated with genotype-dependent differences in lactate transport/clearance during high-intensity exercise; the direction and performance impact are debated and cohort-dependent.

AA.effect_summary: Homozygous MCT1 rs1049434 (Asp490Glu) variant. Associated with genotype-dependent differences in lactate handling, but the direction is debated across cohorts (some studies link this genotype to faster lactate clearance and endurance/power phenotypes, others link the alternate allele), so no firm directional effect is asserted.

snps.recommendation_text: MCT1 (SLC16A1) facilitates lactate transport across cell membranes. rs1049434 (Asp490Glu) is associated with differences in lactate handling during high-intensity exercise, but the allele-direction and performance impact are debated and cohort-dependent — treat as research-grade context, not deterministic recovery advice.

pathways.name: Recovery & Injury
pathways.description: Variants influencing connective tissue integrity, injury susceptibility, and recovery from exercise.

CC.effect_summary: Normal type V collagen expression. Associated with greater musculotendinous flexibility (higher range of motion) and lower tendon/ligament injury risk — the protective genotype at this locus.

CT.effect_summary: One copy of the T allele. Modestly altered type V collagen expression, associated with reduced flexibility (lower range of motion) and increased soft-tissue injury susceptibility.

TC.effect_summary: One copy of the T allele. Modestly altered type V collagen expression, associated with reduced flexibility (lower range of motion) and increased soft-tissue injury susceptibility.

TT.effect_summary: Homozygous T allele. Altered type V collagen expression associated with reduced flexibility (lower range of motion) and higher susceptibility to Achilles tendon and other soft tissue injuries.

snps.recommendation_text: COL5A1 variants have been associated with tendon and ligament injury risk. Individuals with the TT genotype may benefit from gradual training volume increases and targeted tendon-strengthening exercises.

CC.effect_summary: GRCh37 plus-strand C/C, the common G/G genotype in transcript-oriented literature (no T/"s" allele). Baseline, population-average soft-tissue (tendon/ligament) injury risk for this marker, and no COL1A1 Sp1 bone-fragility signal.

CA.effect_summary: GRCh37 plus-strand C/A, the G/T heterozygote in transcript-oriented literature. For sports tendon/ligament injury, meta-analyses suggest the heterozygous genotype may carry the highest soft-tissue injury risk under an overdominant model (e.g. ACL injury); the evidence is mixed and strongest in Caucasian cohorts, so treat this as a soft flag, not a verdict. Separately, the plus-strand A allele (the T/"s" allele in the literature) is associated with modestly lower bone mineral density / higher osteoporotic-fracture risk — a distinct bone-fragility phenotype seen mainly in older/postmenopausal adults, not an athletic stress-fracture prediction.

AC.effect_summary: GRCh37 plus-strand A/C, the T/G heterozygote in transcript-oriented literature. For sports tendon/ligament injury, meta-analyses suggest the heterozygous genotype may carry the highest soft-tissue injury risk under an overdominant model (e.g. ACL injury); the evidence is mixed and strongest in Caucasian cohorts, so treat this as a soft flag, not a verdict. Separately, the plus-strand A allele (the T/"s" allele in the literature) is associated with modestly lower bone mineral density / higher osteoporotic-fracture risk — a distinct bone-fragility phenotype seen mainly in older/postmenopausal adults, not an athletic stress-fracture prediction.

AA.effect_summary: Homozygous GRCh37 plus-strand A/A, the rare T/T ("s/s") genotype in transcript-oriented literature. For sports tendon/ligament injury — this pathway's phenotype — meta-analyses report this genotype is associated with REDUCED (protective) injury risk, including ACL injury, most consistently in Caucasian cohorts; evidence is mixed and protection is not guaranteed. Separately and distinctly, it carries the strongest COL1A1 Sp1 signal for lower bone mineral density and higher osteoporotic (especially vertebral) fracture risk in older/postmenopausal adults — a bone-fragility phenotype that is not an athletic soft-tissue injury risk and is worth attention to bone health with age.

snps.recommendation_text: COL1A1 Sp1 (rs1800012) has phenotype-specific, opposite-direction effects. For sports tendon/ligament injury the rare GRCh37 plus-strand AA genotype (reported as TT in transcript-oriented literature) is generally protective while the heterozygous genotype may carry higher soft-tissue injury risk; separately, the plus-strand A allele (literature T) is linked to lower bone mineral density / osteoporotic fracture risk mainly in older/postmenopausal adults. Tendon/ligament conditioning supports soft-tissue resilience, and weight-bearing exercise with adequate calcium/vitamin D supports bone health with age regardless of genotype.

pathways.name: Training Response
pathways.description: Variants influencing body composition response to exercise, metabolic adaptation, and training-induced fitness gains.

TT.effect_summary: Standard FTO variant. Lower genetic predisposition toward higher BMI.

TA.effect_summary: One copy of risk allele. Modestly higher average BMI (~0.4 kg/m²). Regular physical activity attenuates the effect.

AT.effect_summary: One copy of risk allele. Modestly higher average BMI (~0.4 kg/m²). Regular physical activity attenuates the effect.

AA.effect_summary: Homozygous risk allele. Higher average BMI (~0.7 kg/m²). Physical activity significantly attenuates the genetic effect on body weight.

snps.recommendation_text: FTO is the most replicated obesity-associated gene. Importantly, physical activity significantly reduces the effect of FTO risk alleles on BMI. Regular exercise is beneficial regardless of genotype.

ACTN3_power_context.note: ACTN3 rs1815739 appears under Endurance (XX genotype — no alpha-actinin-3), but is equally relevant to Power (RR genotype — full expression). Genotype frequencies differ between athlete groups at the population level; neither pathway placement asserts an individual power or endurance advantage. The three-state calling model (RR/RX/XX) provides context for both pathways.

ACE_endurance_context.note: ACE rs4341 (I/D proxy) appears under Power (DD -> power context), while II genotype has been reported in some endurance cohorts. Findings display both perspectives with the row-level evidence caveat.

ACTN3_R577X.description: Three-state calling model for ACTN3 R577X. Maps genotype to functional status of alpha-actinin-3 protein.

RR.label: RR — two functional copies
RR.description: Full alpha-actinin-3 expression in fast-twitch muscle fibers. RR is over-represented among sprint/power athletes, but that is a group-level population-frequency association; genotype alone does not predict individual power aptitude.

RX.label: RX — one functional copy
RX.description: One functional copy — alpha-actinin-3 is present, unlike the XX deficiency, at intermediate expression consistent with an additive model. Genotype alone does not predict individual power or endurance aptitude.

XX.label: XX — no functional copies
XX.description: No alpha-actinin-3 protein (alpha-actinin-3 deficiency). XX is consistently under-represented among sprint/power athletes at the group level; a human endurance-performance advantage is NOT established. Context-only, not an endurance call.

ACE_ID_proxy.description: ACE insertion/deletion polymorphism is a 287 bp Alu repeat not directly captured by SNP arrays. rs4341 is used as a proxy SNP in linkage disequilibrium with the I/D variant.
ACE_ID_proxy.proxy_target: ACE I/D (287 bp Alu insertion/deletion in intron 16)
ACE_ID_proxy.proxy_accuracy_note: Published genotyping studies report high linkage disequilibrium between rs4341 and ACE I/D in specific cohorts, but proxy accuracy may vary by ancestry and assay. Results should be interpreted with this caveat.
